ordered_diagnoses: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease

s1.syndrome_frame: subacute onset of respiratory symptoms in a patient with a history of rheumatologic disease and recent initiation of immunosuppressive therapy
salient_findings: ground-glass interstitial infiltrates on chest CT
key_facts: 41-year-old woman
3-month history of sacroiliac pain, arthralgias, and lower-limb myalgias
partial response to NSAIDs
diagnosed with seronegative spondyloarthropathy
negative HLA-B27
bilateral active sacroiliitis on MRI
initiated weekly subcutaneous etanercept 50 mg
significant improvement in joint symptoms
developed respiratory symptoms after the third dose of etanercept
no fever, hemoptysis, chest pain, or other systemic symptoms
afebrile, normal oxygenation on room air
scant basal 'Velcro'-like crackles on pulmonary auscultation
normal laboratory studies except for mild eosinophilia
high-resolution chest CT showed ground-glass interstitial infiltrates
bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage revealed no endobronchial lesions

shortlist.label: Etanercept-induced interstitial lung disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed respiratory symptoms after initiation of etanercept

shortlist.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Ground-glass interstitial infiltrates on chest CT and respiratory symptoms

shortlist.label: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has seronegative spondyloarthropathy and developed interstitial lung disease

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Respiratory symptoms and interstitial infiltrates on chest CT, although less likely given the clinical context

raw.rationale: The patient developed respiratory symptoms after the third dose of etanercept, with high-resolution chest CT showing ground-glass interstitial infiltrates, which is consistent with etanercept-induced interstitial lung disease.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic pneumonia
rejected.why: Mild eosinophilia is present, but the clinical and radiological findings are more consistent with a drug-induced lung injury than eosinophilic pneumonia.

rejected.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and radiological findings could be consistent with cryptogenic organizing pneumonia, but the temporal relationship with etanercept initiation makes drug-induced lung disease more likely.

rejected.label: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease
rejected.why: The patient has seronegative spondyloarthropathy, but the development of respiratory symptoms after etanercept initiation suggests a drug-induced cause rather than a disease-associated interstitial lung disease.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of lymphadenopathy, granulomas, or other systemic symptoms typical of sarcoidosis, making this diagnosis less likely.
